text: Anantnag district is an administrative district in the Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, located in the disputed Kashmir region and one of ten districts comprising the Kashmir Valley. Its headquarters is the city of Anantnag. As of the 2011 census, it was the third most populous district in Jammu and Kashmir (out of 22), following Jammu and Srinagar. The district includes six tehsils—Anantnag, Bijbehara, Dooru, Kokernag, Pahalgam, and Shangus—and is divided into seven blocks: Breng, Shangus, Achabal, Dachnipora, Qazigund, Khoveripora, and Shahabad. It covers a total area of 3,574 square kilometres (1,380 sq mi) and is bordered by Kargil and Kishtwar to the east, Doda and Ramban to the south, Ganderbal to the north, and Kulgam, Srinagar, Pulwama, and Shopian to the west. Anantnag has a moderate climate (Köppen classification), characterized by cool springs and autumns, mild summers, and cold winters, influenced by the Karakoram to the east and the Pirpanjal range to the south. The hilly eastern areas are cooler than the flat northern regions. Summer is mild with high humidity and cool nights, and precipitation occurs throughout the year, with July being the hottest month (mean max 32°C, mean min 6°C) and December–January the coldest (mean max 0°C, mean min −15°C). The record high is 33°C and the record low is −18°C. On 5–6 January 2012, heavy snowfall and low temperatures led to a state of emergency, with school closures on 6 and 7 January. Over recent years, there has been an increase in relative humidity and annual precipitation, likely due to commercial afforestation projects that expanded parks and green cover, making suburban areas more lush than the central region. The district shares the typical climate of the Kashmir Valley, as described by Pandit Kulan or Kalhana, who noted the mild sunshine, saffron, iced water, and grapes, and compared it to places like Peshawar, Baghdad, Damascus, Fez, and South Carolina, though it does not match any single climate. Sir Walter Lawrence observed that every hundred feet of elevation brings a new climate and vegetation phase. Anantnag has seven assembly constituencies: Anantnag, Anantnag West, Dooru, Kokernag, Shangus-Anantnag East, Bijbehara, and Pahalgam, and one Lok Sabha constituency. The current Member of Parliament for Anantnag-Rajouri is Mian Altaf Ahmed Larvi of the JKNC, and the District Development Commissioner (DDC) is Yousuf Gorsi of the JKNC, part of the PAGD. According to the 2011 census, the district had a population of 1,078,692, roughly equivalent to the nation of Cyprus or the U.S. state of Rhode Island, ranking 425th in India (out of 640). The population density is 375 inhabitants per square kilometre (970/sq mi), with a 37.48% growth rate between 2001 and 2011. The sex ratio is 927 females per 1,000 males (varying by religion), and the literacy rate is 64.32%. About 26.23% of the population lives in urban areas, with Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes constituting 0.17% and 10.75% of the population, respectively. Anantnag city, with a population of 108,505, is the largest city in the district, and the Anantnag Urban Agglomeration has a population of 158,785. Kashmiri is the predominant language, spoken by 85.10% of the population, followed by Gujari at 11.46% and Pahari at 1.21%. The nearest airport is Sheikh ul-Alam International Airport in Srinagar, 60 kilometres from Anantnag, and there is an Indian Air Force airbase in Awantipora. The district is well-connected by rail, with the Jammu–Baramulla line passing through it and numerous railway stations. It is also well-connected by roads, including NH 44, NH 244, and NH 501, which run through the district alongside other intra-district roads.
